prompt: Where does a Cloud Billing account sit relative to the resource hierarchy?
hint: It pays for projects in any folder.

choices.text: Under the organisation, above the folders
choices.why: It is not a node of the tree at all.
Right. One billing account may pay for projects anywhere in the tree, or in several organisations.

choices.text: Inside each project, one per project
choices.why: Many projects can share one account; it is linked, not contained.

choices.text: In the folder `shared`, with the logs
choices.why: Folders hold projects, never billing accounts.

prompt: Which role is the one to keep scarce, according to the lesson, and why?
hint: Which role spends the company's money?

choices.why: Reading costs spends nothing.
Budgets warn; they spend nothing either.
That is a project role and touches no billing account.
Right. Whoever can link projects to the account can run anything on the company's card.

prompt: An accountant must see every cost and invoice, across all projects, and nothing inside them. Which grant fits?
hint: A role on the account, not on projects.

choices.why: Right. It shows the money and nothing the money paid for.
That shows every resource, which the accountant does not need.
Admin can change payment methods and close the account.
That is the widest grant there is, for a reading job.

prompt: Match each billing role to what it allows.

pairs.right: payment methods and closing the account

prompt: How does a self-serve billing account pay?

choices.text: A monthly invoice paid by transfer
choices.why: That is an invoiced, or offline, account.
Credits reduce a bill; they are not how the account pays.
Right. Invoiced accounts are the other kind, after a credit check.
Workspace is billed separately from Cloud Billing.

prompt: To link a project to a billing account, what does the caller need?

choices.why: Owner covers the project side; the account must allow it too.
That covers the account side; the project must allow it too.
Right. `billing.user` on the account, and Owner or Project Billing Manager on the project.

choices.text: Nothing; any project may link to any account
choices.why: Then anybody could spend anybody's money.

prompt: In `billing.tf`, which piece of the file makes the link?

choices.why: Right. The link is part of the project's description.
That grants a role on the account; it links nothing.
Labels are counted; they do not link.
Folders have no billing link; it is per project.

prompt: A team unlinks `planner-staging` from its billing account over a weekend to 'save money'. What can they find on Monday?
hint: Unlinking stops paid services; what happens to stored data?

choices.text: Everything as it was, minus the weekend's bill
choices.why: That is what stopping things deliberately gives. Unlinking is harsher.

choices.text: The project moved to another billing account
choices.why: Nothing re-links a project on its own.

choices.text: The project deleted, with a thirty-day undelete
choices.why: Unlinking does not delete the project itself.

choices.text: Machines stopped, and stored data at risk of deletion
choices.why: Right. Unlinking is not a pause; resources that cost money to keep may be deleted.

prompt: `gcloud billing accounts list` was refused. Which service refused it?

choices.why: The emulator is Pub/Sub only, and the override covers only Pub/Sub.
Right. The Cloud Billing API, which answers only authenticated callers.
That owns projects; billing accounts are another API.
The command was `gcloud`, and the refusal came from Google.

prompt: A billing account id has three groups of ___ characters, such as `012345-6789AB-CDEF01`.
A virtual machine in `planner-prod` sends backups to Santiago. Which project pays for the traffic?

choices.why: Right. Traffic is billed to the project of the machine that sends it.

choices.text: The project that receives the backups
choices.why: The receiver pays nothing for traffic coming in.
No such split exists; the sender pays.

choices.text: The billing account, outside any project
choices.why: Traffic is a project's cost, paid through its account.

prompt: With a shared network in `planner-network`, a team reading only `planner-prod`'s costs misses a charge. Which?
hint: What belongs to the network itself?

choices.why: Disks stay with the machines' project.
The sender's project pays that, which is `planner-prod`.

choices.text: The Cloud NAT gateway its traffic goes through
choices.why: Right. Resources of the network are billed to the host project.
Topics are billed to the project they live in.

prompt: A manager wants one billing account per team so that each team's costs are separate. What does the lesson suggest instead?
hint: Separating costs is a reading job.

choices.why: That splits the whole estate to split a bill.
Right. Labels split costs inside one bill without moving any project.

choices.text: One project per team, all unlinked
choices.why: Unlinked projects run nothing that costs money.

choices.text: A budget per team on separate cards
choices.why: Budgets do not move costs between cards.

prompt: A report sums every cost line of the month and ignores credits. What is wrong with its total?

choices.text: It is lower than the bill
choices.why: Credits subtract; ignoring them can only add.
Credits are applied on the same bill, as negative lines.

choices.text: It counts the free tier twice
choices.why: Nothing is counted twice; something is left out.

choices.text: It is higher than the bill
choices.why: Right. Credits reduce the costs they apply to; leaving them out overstates.

prompt: A machine in `planner-prod` sends 200 GiB a month to Santiago. At the price read in lesson 1, how many dollars does `planner-prod` pay for it?
A developer creates a project and runs an expensive experiment on the company's card, though nobody gave them a role on production. What made it possible?
hint: Which role spends money without touching production?

choices.text: Owner on their own new project
choices.why: Owner covers the project side; without a role on the account it could not link.
Knowing the id links nothing.
Labels decide nothing, money included.
Right. With it, any project they own can be linked to the company's account.
